about: Dom 2026-10-26 (after /physics1 on his iPhone: five ragdolls + a cut, 0.40 ms a frame): the opponent's body is a physics ragdoll (@frankendom/physics, Jolt WASM, package.json) for PRESENTATION only. The 60 Hz sim (src/fight/duel.ts) and Gate 0 never see it, and nothing it does goes back into the sim. src/fight/ragdoll.ts reads every number and name here. `on`: default on; `?<query>=<v1>` (?physics=v1) = today's death and hit behaviour exactly (the chunk is never fetched). `opponents`: the opponent ids that get a ragdoll, each with the body file it is drawn in (src/assets/<body>.glb), its rig (a key of `rigs`) and its body measure row (`measure`: a site path the build copies from the package's data/bodies/, fetched with the chunk). `rigs`: the package's 20 part ids -> the bone names on that rig (one map per rig, so the Minotaur's later 106 rig is one more row). `tickHz` / `maxTicksPerFrame`: the fixed physics step in the scene's own accumulator, beside the sim's. `seed`: the physics world's seed (the engine draws nothing; kept for the package's rand()). `loadAfterFirstFrameMs`: the chunk is imported this long after the first frame, so it never competes with the first visit. `hit`: a landed blow (sim event Hit, the opponent the target) -> the part its location strikes, the impulse (N s) along the attacker's facing plus `lift` up, and the stagger: motor strength per role (`targets`, the package's role keys; 1 = full) eased in over `easeInS`, held `holdS`, back over `upS` (Physics Dev's brief: arm 0.9 / torso 0.6 / hand 0.12, hold 0.5 s, back over 0.35 s; legs at the torso value, as the package's states.json reads it). `blend`: how much of the ragdoll's pose the bones show at the dip's deepest; 0 (2026-10-26): the stagger only primes the ragdoll and the animation alone is on screen, because the motors lag a fast clip (measured in the fight at 375, full motors, kinematic hips: median 0.3 rad off the clip on the upper arms and 0.8-1.2 on forearms and hands, p95 1.5-2.9; spine 0.1-0.25): any visible share showed an arm flung out mid-swing, which read as a glitch, not a stagger. `kill`: the killing blow (sim event Killed): part by location, impulse along the attacker's facing plus `lift`; the bones go from the death clip's pose to the ragdoll's over `blendInS` (so that lag never pops on the killing frame); then the package's death ramp (1 -> 0.01 over 1 s) and the bones follow the ragdoll until it sleeps; the corpse stays down until the rematch. `plainDeathOnly`: a cinematic finisher (Split Crown, Decapitation, Run Through, Opened) plays exactly as before and gets no ragdoll; only the plain death (the rotation's no-ceremony outcome, kick and skill kills) falls as a ragdoll.
